newsitem.title: UK: UK building societies bill set to become law.
newsitem.headline: UK building societies bill set to become law.

text.p: The Building Societies Bill is virtually certain to be passed before parliament is prorogued on Friday, political sources said on Tuesday.
They said the bill is expected to go through all its stages in the House of Lords on Wednesday without being amended, meaning it will need minimal time to become law.

The bill, which has cross-party support, would remove certain restrictions on mutually owned building societies, allowing them to compete more effectively with societies that convert to banks with the status of public limited companies.
"There will be no problem with that bill," a Labour source said.

Leader of the House of Commons Tony Newton told MPs on Tuesday night that he had come to an agreement with the opposition Labour Party on the Education Bill, one of the most contentious measures being considered by parliament.
He said the government would withdraw clauses providing for the expansion of grammar and grant-maintained schools and for increased selection by schools.

"We are pleased that we have agreement to proceed with all of the measures in the bill on discipline and standards...we shall come back to the selection and GM (grant maintained) regulation matters at the earliest possible opportunity," he said.
